title: Sensex jumps 898 points to nine-month high as banks lead; rupee strengthens past 93
dek: The Nifty closed at 25,800.60 as foreign money rotated out of AI stocks in Asia and into India; the rupee rose for a fifth day.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Sensex rose 897.96 points, or 1.08 per cent, to close at 83,919.71 on Friday, and the Nifty gained 286.30 points, or 1.12 per cent, to 25,800.60, as bank shares led a second straight day of strong gains and Indian shares outperformed a sharp sell-off elsewhere in Asia, according to reports. Both indices closed at their highest levels in about nine months.

The rupee strengthened for a fifth straight session, closing at about 92.67 to the US dollar, its strongest in about seven months, according to reports. It had ended Thursday at 93.36.

## What moved

Banks did most of the work. The Nifty Private Bank index rose about 3 per cent and the Nifty Bank index about 2.5 per cent; IndusInd Bank jumped 8.6 per cent, and Axis Bank (up 4.7 per cent) and HDFC Bank (up 2.9 per cent) were among the biggest Nifty gainers, along with Apollo Hospitals (up 5.3 per cent), Max Healthcare and Maruti Suzuki, reports said. Information technology shares rose 1.3 per cent. Titan, Tata Steel, NTPC and Hindustan Unilever were the main losers, and the media index fell nearly 2 per cent.

The gains were narrow: on the BSE, 2,456 shares fell and 1,582 rose, and the India VIX volatility index climbed 7.5 per cent, according to reports. Markets had opened lower, with the Sensex down more than 600 points early on, before recovering in the afternoon.

## Why India is outperforming

Analysts said global investors were moving money out of shares tied to artificial intelligence and semiconductors, which have fallen heavily this week, and into markets with little AI exposure, such as India. Asian shares had their worst week since March 2020, with Japan, South Korea and Taiwan hit hardest, according to reports. Foreign portfolio investors have put a record of about $12.2 billion into Indian shares so far in November, after heavy outflows over the previous two years, reports said.

Cheaper oil has also helped. Brent crude has fallen about 23 per cent in November on hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Iran conflict and a recovery in shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, according to reports. India imports most of its oil, so lower prices ease pressure on inflation and the rupee.

Nagaraj Shetti of HDFC Securities said the "underlying trend of Nifty remains sharply positive", and that the index could move towards 26,000 in the next one to two weeks, according to reports.

## What happens next

Markets reopen on Monday. Investors will watch whether foreign buying continues, the direction of AI-linked stocks in the US after this week's sell-off, and oil prices. Figures are provisional and based on exchange closing data as reported; reports differ slightly on Thursday's rupee close.
